Empirical Research Plan  
“Spillovers from Sudden Severe Health Events within Families and Workplaces”

-----------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-----------------------------------------------------------
Method: Difference-in-Differences (panel event-study).

Justification  
a)  The health shock (first non-fatal AMI or stroke; unexpected death) is plausibly exogenous in timing.  
b)  We observe the same potential “treated” individual both before and after the shock as well as an otherwise comparable counterfactual individual whose network member has not yet (or never) experienced the shock.  
c)  Monthly/annual registers covering the full population allow very rich fixed effects and dynamic leads/lags, making an event-study the natural design.  
d)  The question explicitly requires tracing dynamics and mechanisms (learning vs salience); the event-study coefficients γk supply those trajectories.

-----------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-----------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
T_i,t  = 1 in year (or month) t and thereafter if ego i’s network member j (spouse, child, in-law, coworker) experiences her FIRST severe health event in t.  
Separate treatment dummies are created for each network layer.

Treatment timing  
Event date = date of hospital admission for AMI/stroke OR date of death (fatal sample).  
We collapse to the ego’s calendar month (preferred) or calendar year.

Control group (stacked-DiD)  
•  Primary: “Future treated” – individuals whose comparable network member will suffer the same type of shock but only in the future (t + 2 or more).  
•  Secondary: Individuals whose comparable network member never has the shock during the sample window (used in robustness checks, acknowledging potential selection).

Why future-treated? It aligns pre-trend composition and eliminates concerns that households prone to health shocks differ systematically.

Sample inclusion  
Drop observations for any ego who receives her own AMI/stroke in the –12 to +12 month window around spouse’s event to isolate spillovers.

-----------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-----------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends / common shocks  
Absent the spouse’s (or coworker’s) event, health-care utilization trajectories of treated and control egos would have evolved in parallel.  
Plausibility: Future-treated controls share observed and unobserved risk factors. Denmark’s universal health care minimizes differential insurance shocks.

A2. No anticipation (or at least no anticipatory change before the recorded admission/death).  
Heart attacks and strokes are sudden; severe cancer deaths more predictable, so we will test for leads and trim anticipatory horizons where needed.

A3. Stable unit composition (no differential mortality/emigration that removes egos from the sample differentially post-treatment).  
We can verify using survival/emigration outcomes and inverse-probability weights.

A4. SUTVA / no spillovers across comparison groups  
If both spouses of a couple suffer events at different times, the second ego is removed from control pool. We cluster at the family or workplace level to allow arbitrary intra-cluster correlation.

-----------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Remedies
-----------------------------------------------------------
Threat 1. Simultaneous shocks to the ego (e.g., shared lifestyle or stress leads the spouse and ego to have correlated infarctions).  
Remedy: (i) Exclude egos with own hospitalization ±12 months, (ii) control flexibly for ego’s time-varying comorbidities captured in registers.

Threat 2. Psychological grief or caregiving burden rather than information/salience.  
Remedy: Compare non-health-related outcomes (e.g., alcohol purchases, mental-health visits) to separate stress from learning; heterogeneous effects by distance (coworker vs spouse) help differentiate channels.

Threat 3. Differential censoring due to death or migration.  
Remedy: Competing-risks models, IPW, and robustness restricting to egos surviving three years post-event.

-----------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-----------------------------------------------------------
```r
#----------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
#----------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(lubridate)
library(fixest)    # fast high-dimensional FE
library(did)       # Callaway-Sant’Anna for staggered adoption
#----------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and merge registers
#----------------------------------------------------------
hh   <- fread("household_panel_1985_2011.csv")     # demographics
hosp <- fread("hospital_events_1980_2011.csv")     # ICD diagnoses
rx   <- fread("prescription_1995_2011.csv")        # ATC codes
prim <- fread("primarycare_1985_2011.csv")         # GP/specialist

# Example variable construction: spouse’s first AMI
hosp[, ami := (icd %in% c("410","I21","I22"))]     # ICD-8/10 mapping
hosp[, event_date := ymd(adm_date)]
setorder(hosp, pid, event_date)
ami_first <- hosp[ami==TRUE, .SD[1], by = pid]     # first AMI per person

# Create spouse-event file
spouse_link <- fread("spouse_links.csv")           # ego-spouse pairs
sp_event <- merge(spouse_link, ami_first,
                  by.x="spouse_id", by.y="pid", all.x = TRUE)

# Collapse to ego-year panel 1995-2011 (statin availability)
years <- 1995:2011
panel <- CJ(pid = unique(spouse_link$ego_id), year = years)
panel <- merge(panel, hh, by=c("pid","year"), all.x=TRUE)
panel <- merge(panel, sp_event[,.(ego_id, event_year = year(event_date))],
               by.x="pid", by.y="ego_id", all.x=TRUE)

# Treatment dummy and leads/lags (event time)
panel[, rel_year := year - event_year]           # -k … +k
panel[, treat := as.integer(year >= event_year & !is.na(event_year))]

# Outcome: any statin purchase in year
rx[, year := year(date)]
statin_codes <- c("C10AA","C10AB","C10AC","C10AD")
statin_use <- rx[ATC %in% statin_codes, .(statin=1), by=.(pid,year)]
panel <- merge(panel, statin_use, by=c("pid","year"), all.x=TRUE)
panel[is.na(statin), statin:=0]

#----------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Main DiD specification (two-way FE + dynamic leads/lags)
#----------------------------------------------------------
# Create event-time dummies, omitting -1 as base
for(k in -5:5){
  if(k==-1) next
  panel[, paste0("d",k) := as.integer(rel_year==k)]
}

formula_dyn <- as.formula(
  "statin ~ d-5 + d-4 + d-3 + d-2 + d0 + d1 + d2 + d3 + d4 + d5 |
            pid + year"
)

est <- feols(formula_dyn, data = panel, cluster = ~household_id)
etable(est, se = "cluster")

#----------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Robustness: Callaway-Sant’Anna allowing heterogeneous timing
#----------------------------------------------------------
cs <- att_gt(yname="statin",
             tname="year",
             idname="pid",
             gname="event_year",       # first treatment year
             xformla = ~ age + educ,
             data = panel[year >= 1995 & year <= 2011])
agg_effect <- aggte(cs, type="dynamic")
summary(agg_effect)
```

-----------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-----------------------------------------------------------
Direction: Positive take-up of preventive care among egos after a spouse’s AMI/stroke.  
Magnitude (statins): Baseline annual statin use for 50-64-year-olds in early-2000s Denmark ≈ 10 %. I expect a 2–4 pp (20-40 %) increase within two years after the spouse’s event, tapering thereafter. For adult children, perhaps half that size; for coworkers, <1 pp.

-----------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)  
(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)
C1. Parallel pre-trends verified with event-study leads …………… 1  
C2. No anticipatory behavior ………………………………………… 0.5 (some cancers)  
C3. No spillovers to controls ………………………………………… 0.5 (possible multi-layer links)  
C4. No differential attrition ………………………………………… 1  
C5. Accurate treatment timing ……………………………………… 1  
Total = 4/5

-----------------------------------------------------------
End of plan
